target.title: feat(talk): durable client voice sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice conversations in Talk are ephemeral today. A client-owned realtime call (iOS WebRTC, the Control UI, or a gateway-relay fallback) speaks directly to the provider; if the transport drops, everything said is lost, nothing lands in the agent's chat history, and any tool action the voice model triggers leaves no trail. This makes voice a second-class surface: you can't scroll back through a call, other clients never see it, and there's no record of what a voice request changed.

This change makes a voice call **part of your normal agent session** across every client that can run Talk, and adds a safety gate for high-impact actions requested by voice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The design deliberately reuses existing session machinery instead of a parallel store:

- **Voice utterances live-append into the canonical agent session transcript.** A Talk consult is already a plain `chat.send` on the agent's main session, so finalized user/assistant utterances are appended as ordinary transcript messages (idempotent by a `voice:<voiceSessionId>:<entryId>` event id). They show up in web chat and every other connected client, and later consults see them as normal history — no transcript-threading or import step.
  - Client-owned transports (iOS WebRTC, Control UI) report finalized utterances via the new `talk.client.transcript` RPC.
  - Gateway-relay sessions record server-side at the existing final-transcript seam, so **Android and every relay fallback get durable voice history with no client changes**.
- **A small per-agent SQLite call record** (in the agent cache DB — no schema bump) tracks the logical call across transport restarts, the consult runs it spawned, and which mutating tools ran. It powers reconnect continuity, abandoned-call recovery, and the post-call summary.
- **Run-scoped spoken confirmation** pauses high-impact tools (message send, node/gateway/browser/computer control, cron, destructive shell, publication) invoked by a voice-originated run until the user gives an exact spoken "yes". Approval binds to a sha256 fingerprint of the tool+args and is consumed once, so the model can't confirm one action and run another. Concurrent non-voice runs on the same session are unaffected. Capability is negotiated explicitly (clients declare `voice-transcript`), so deployed clients that predate this protocol keep prior behavior rather than getting stuck at an unconfirmable pause.
- **Provider profile context** (the existing bounded IDENTITY/USER/SOUL bundle that Discord voice already injects) is added to the realtime provider session, scoped to the bound agent.
- **A mutation-only "Voice call changes" digest** is delivered to the session's last non-WebChat channel when a call that changed something ends.

**Zero new configuration** — everything is always on. No `openclaw.json` fields, env vars, or CLI flags were added.

This supersedes the durable-voice-session direction from #109376 (thanks @clifton, credited as co-author); the reshaped architecture live-appends into the session rather than maintaining a parallel ledger, keys confirmation by the consult run rather than the shared session, negotiates transcript capability explicitly, and drops the `--legacy-direct-auth` credential-in-QR workaround.

## User Impact

- Voice calls appear in your agent session history on every client, live, and survive transport drops (reconnect resumes the same logical call).
- Abandoned calls (app killed mid-call) are recovered and their transcript imported on your next call.
- High-impact actions asked for by voice require an explicit spoken confirmation before they run.
- After a call that changed something, you get a short "Voice call changes" summary on your usual channel.
- No configuration or migration for operators; existing config is untouched. Cross-client (iOS/web/relay/Android); macOS has no realtime voice today and is unchanged.
- Two new additive gateway RPCs (`talk.client.transcript`, `talk.client.close`) and optional `voiceSessionId`/`capabilities` fields on existing Talk methods; generated Swift/Kotlin/TS clients are regenerated. Server-owned relay/managed-room responses keep `voiceSessionId` optional so older gateways/clients interoperate.

## Evidence

- New/changed Vitest coverage across the confirmation gate, SQLite call record, transcript append/dedup, relay persistence, protocol scopes, and the Control UI transcript queue: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/talk/client-voice-session.test.ts src/talk/client-voice-confirmation.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/talk-client.test.ts src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-tool.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-consult.test.ts` — all pass (178 focused tests).
- Protocol generators regenerated with no tracked drift: `scripts/protocol-gen.ts`, `protocol-gen-swift.ts`, `protocol-gen-kotlin.ts`.
- `git diff --check` clean; docs updated (`docs/nodes/talk.md`, `docs/gateway/protocol.md`).
- Iterated under repeated adversarial autoreview (codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh) covering the confirmation-gate safety paths, transcript-loss and cross-agent-leak cases, and lifecycle races; remaining accepted tradeoffs (the informational digest is best-effort, and confirmation state is process-local like the rest of the subsystem) are documented in-code.
- The mutation digest is intentionally best-effort informational; the authoritative effects live on the call record and the canonical transcript is persisted independently.

Full CI/Testbox proof will be attached from the PR run.
